routes.title: Use a supported remote machine, or treat on-device inference as experimental
routes.summary: Official Android Ollama support is not established. Learn Termux first; run a local model on your own supported computer over SSH if available.
routes.cost: Local hardware or remote-host costs; no promised on-phone route.

routes.title: Start on Android with a browser terminal or SSH
routes.summary: Use Termux for Git and SSH, or a browser environment for supported Linux tools. Native agent binaries need individual compatibility checks.
routes.cost: Cloud compute and provider inference have separate quotas/costs.

routes.title: Local to the cloud host is still remote from your device
routes.summary: Check the host memory and policy. For private on-device inference, use your own supported computer instead of a hosted terminal.
routes.cost: Cloud-host compute/storage may be billed even without a model API.

routes.title: Try a small local model for focused learning
routes.summary: Begin with a tiny explanation task and short context. Low memory is a serious constraint; do not expect autonomous repository editing.
routes.cost: No local inference API fee; hardware, download, and electricity costs remain.

routes.title: Ollama + a compatible coding client
routes.summary: Start with Aider and one model that fits your available memory. Use a tool-capable model for autonomous agents and review every edit.
routes.cost: Local inference uses your hardware; choose explicit local tags.

routes.title: Check current legitimate cloud allowances
routes.summary: Review Antigravity account eligibility and OpenRouter free-model availability. Neither is unlimited or a guaranteed entitlement.
routes.cost: Free-tier limits apply; inspect paid fallback and compute costs.

routes.title: OpenRouter + Aider or OpenCode
routes.summary: Choose an exact model ID, inspect its price and privacy policy, and load your own key securely.
routes.cost: Model-specific free or metered API usage.

routes.title: Choose a documented cloud provider and one agent
routes.summary: Use an eligible official account or your own API key. Make a small read-only request before granting edits or shell actions.
routes.cost: Account allowance or paid API; open-source software is a separate property.
